\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Threshold Functions --- Sparse Sampling}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.SparseSampling
\section{Overview}
Finite independent sampling and uniform concentration give a signed-character approximation to any nonzero real cube function, controlled by its spectral one-norm.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[One-sided concentration of bounded independent samples]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sample_tail}
\leanok
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p117-b005}
\difficulty{5}
Let $s>0$ be an integer and $Y_1,\ldots,Y_s$ be independent real functions on a probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$, each measurable up to a null set and valued in $[-1,1]$ almost surely, with common mean $\mathbb E Y_i=m$. Write $\Pr(A)=\mu^*(A)$ for outer probability. For every real $\varepsilon\ge0$, $\Pr[s\varepsilon\le\sum_iY_i-sm]\le\exp(-s\varepsilon^2/2)$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $s$ be a positive integer, and let
$Y_1,\ldots,Y_s$ be independent real-valued random variables that are measurable up to
null sets, take values in $[-1,1]$ almost surely, and have common mean $m$. For every
$\varepsilon\ge 0$, the probability that $\left|\sum_{i=1}^s Y_i-sm\right|\ge
s\varepsilon$ is at most $2\exp(-s\varepsilon^2/2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential bound for positive dimension]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_numeric}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every positive integer $n$, $2^{n+1}e^{-2n}<1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sample size exponent bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_param}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,s$ be nonnegative integers and let $L,\delta>0$. If $4nL^2/\delta^2\le s$, then
$2n\le s(\delta/L)^2/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Concentration sum below one]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_union_numeric}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_numeric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_param}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $s$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $L,\delta>0$.
If $4nL^2/\delta^2\le s$, then $2^n\bigl(2\exp(-s(\delta/L)^2/2)\bigr)<1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A point outside a finite family of small events]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.exists_good_of_union_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $\beta$ be a finite set, and assign an
arbitrary subset $A_b\subseteq\Omega$ to each $b\in\beta$. If $B\in\mathbb R$ satisfies
$\mu^*(A_b)\le B$ for every $b$ and $|\beta|B<1$, where $\mu^*$ is the outer measure
induced by $\mu$, then there is a point of $\Omega$ belonging to none of the sets $A_b$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. Write $\widehat
f(S)$ for the Fourier–Walsh coefficient of $f$ at $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let
$L=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}|\widehat f(S)|$. If $L>0$, there is a probability
distribution $\pi$ on the subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that, for every
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$, the expectation over $S\sim\pi$ of $\operatorname{sgn}_+(\widehat
f(S))\chi_S(x)$ equals $f(x)/L$, where $\operatorname{sgn}_+(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$
for $t<0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of the spectral one-norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.spectralOneNorm_pos}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.spectralOneNorm, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.spectralOneNorm_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function that is not
identically zero. Then its spectral one-norm is strictly positive:
$\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|\widehat f(S)|>0$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be nonzero. Write
$\widehat f(S)$ for the Fourier–Walsh coefficient at $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and set
$L=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}|\widehat f(S)|$. For $\delta>0$ and a nonnegative
integer $s$ with $4nL^2/\delta^2\le s$, there exist subsets
$T_1,\ldots,T_s\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with repetitions allowed, such that for every
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$, $\left|f(x)-\sum_{j=1}^s \frac{L}{s}\operatorname{sgn}_+(\widehat
f(T_j))\chi_{T_j}(x)\right|<\delta$, where $\operatorname{sgn}_+(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and
$-1$ for $t<0$.
\end{theorem}
